subject: Banking
title: The Credit Score Myth
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Credit Score Myth usable.

hook.text: Avoiding your score for fear of damage is like avoiding a scale because you want to lose weight.

buildup.text: Soft inquiries like checking your own score or employer checks don't affect it.

discovery.text: A hard inquiry drops your score 5-10 points. But rate shopping for a mortgage within 14-45 days counts as only one.

twist.text: 50 million Americans have never checked their credit report.

climax.text: Not checking your score is riskier than checking it. Errors and fraud go undetected when nobody looks.

punchline.text: Checking your score won't lower it. Not checking is the real risk.

quiz.question: Does checking your own credit score lower it?
options: No, self-checks are soft inquiries that don't affect your score

details.summary: The credit score myth is the belief that a high score means you are financially healthy. In reality, credit scores measure debt management, not wealth. Someone deeply in debt with perfect payments has a higher score than a debt-free person with no credit history.
details.whyItMatters: Conflating credit scores with financial health leads people to take on debt they do not need. Understanding what scores actually measure helps make smarter decisions about when to build credit versus when to prioritize other financial goals.
takeaways: Credit scores measure debt management, not wealth or financial health
A person with zero debt may have no credit score at all
Optimizing for score can conflict with optimizing for financial wellbeing

faq.question: Can you have a good financial life with no credit score?
faq.answer: Yes, but with limitations. Without a score, you may need manual underwriting for a mortgage, cannot easily rent apartments, and may face higher insurance rates. Some people avoid credit entirely and work around these barriers successfully.

faq.question: Should you go into debt just to build a credit score?
faq.answer: No. Use a credit card for purchases you would make anyway and pay the full balance monthly. This builds excellent credit without paying interest or creating debt. The score is a tool for cheaper borrowing, not a goal in itself.
